what_happened: The job to split process-lifecycle code out of drain.rs was rejected at the final verdict. One of 5 acceptance criteria was unmet: drain.rs must have fewer than 1500 production lines and a new drain/lifecycle.rs must hold the moved code. There were three blocker or major findings. The blocker: drain.rs is still about 4013 production lines, far above the 1500 limit and the 2000 absolute limit. One major finding: the request's line count was stale, and neither the reading nor the producer re-measured the file before planning or finishing. The other major finding: the accepted reading did not match the request, so passing criteria did not show the request was met. No checks are listed as failed.
cause: The request quoted a file size taken at some earlier time, and nothing resolves such numbers against the current snapshot before the reading is accepted. The reading and the plan inherited the stale figure, so the planned slice was too small to reach the limit. The producer was also not required to measure the file before and after the move and report the number against the target. The measurable goal, a line count under the limit, was only checked by the verifier at the end. The wrong premise therefore survived reading, planning and production.
prevention: Add a code check that runs when a reading is accepted. For any request that names a size or line-count target, it measures the named files in the current snapshot and records the measured values in the reading. It refuses or flags the reading if the stated figure differs from the measurement. Require the producer to re-measure after the split and attach the numbers, so a shortfall is seen before the verifier runs. Both steps are code, not prompt wording. Gate counts show no disagreements for any gate, so relax or remove does not apply.
proposed_request: Split the process-lifecycle code out of crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs into a new crates/athena-cli/src/drain/lifecycle.rs. First measure the production lines of drain.rs now (test modules excluded) and record the number. drain.rs is currently about 4013 production lines, and an earlier figure in a request was stale. Outcome: drain.rs has fewer than 1500 production lines (test modules excluded), and lifecycle.rs holds the moved code. If one pass cannot reach 1500, move the largest cohesive groups first (process lifecycle, then the next largest) and report the before and after line counts. Behavior must not change: cargo test, clippy and fmt pass. The final report must state the measured line counts of drain.rs and lifecycle.rs.
